questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The life and work of Johannes Gutenberg
Printers that build solid objects
Why paper books are still popular
How to fix a laser printer at home
questions.why: They discuss 3D printers, which build solid objects, and the problems they solve.

options: By cutting away material from a block
By pressing wooden blocks into ink
By pouring material into a mould
By adding material layer by layer
questions.why: Neil says they build up objects by adding material layer on layer, unlike a sculptor.

questions.q: According to Professor Mark Miodownik, why did 3D printers become cheap after 2000?
options: Patents ran out, so cheap ones appeared
The government paid for them in schools
New materials were discovered in labs
Schools started building their own
questions.why: He says as the millennium turned, patents expired and people started making very cheap 3D printers.

questions.q: What did people discover 3D printers were especially good for?
options: Printing local newspapers quickly
Making test models of new products
Building cheap houses very quickly
Replacing teachers in classrooms
questions.why: He says 'it's actually really great for prototyping'.

questions.q: What does Professor Miodownik suggest happened when people got excited?
options: They stopped using the printers after a while
They sold them to hospitals and schools
They thought it would solve everything
They made them much more expensive
questions.why: He says it became 'the answer to everything. Everything was going to be 3D-printed!'

questions.q: What did Stephen Verze's 3D-printed eye do for him?
options: It gave him back his sight in that eye
It helped him see better in the dark
It stopped the pain in his eye for good
It boosted his confidence, not his sight
questions.why: Sam says it doesn't restore his sight, but it has boosted his confidence.

questions.q: According to surgeon Mandeep Sagoo, what is the problem with the traditional way of making artificial eyes?
options: It takes a lot of time and skill
It is only available in poor countries
The eyes never match
It uses dangerous materials
questions.why: He says it's an artisan process which is very time-consuming and requires real artistry.

questions.q: How long can 3D printing now take to complete the process?
options: Several weeks
Two days
Thirty minutes
Five hours
questions.why: Neil says 3D printing can complete the whole process in just thirty minutes.
